description:
Compare the AIDE methodology artifacts in this project against the canonical versions and return structured JSON results grouped by category. Use this when the user asks to update AIDE, sync AIDE, refresh AIDE, check for AIDE updates, or bring AIDE up to date. This is NOT for editing user .aide specs — it inspects methodology infrastructure only.

The tool uses a two-call pattern for progressive disclosure:

**First call (no `category` param):** Returns a lightweight summary — every category with file names, statuses, and counts, but NO file content. Use this to understand what has drifted and present a summary to the user. Ask which categories they want to apply.

**Second call (with `category` param):** The tool writes all differs/missing files directly to disk itself and returns a manifest — file results with `filePath`, `status` (`"updated"`, `"created"`, or `"unchanged"`), and `name`, but NO `canonicalContent`. The agent never sees file content and never uses the Write tool for methodology files.

Repeat the second call for each category the user confirms.

As the calling agent, you must:
1. Call without `category` first to get the summary
2. Present each drifted category (differs/missing) and ask the user which to apply
3. For each confirmed category, call again with `category=X` — the tool writes the files and returns a manifest. Report what was updated/created to the user.
4. For the `mcp` category, a result that carries `prescription` is merged into the existing MCP config by you (read → merge → write). A result that carries `pinMove` or `globalSwitch` is never merged by hand: the tool writes it (see the MCP step). If `malformed`, tell the user — do not overwrite.
5. For `ide`, the manifest may include `instructions` for VS Code extension install — execute that command for the user. Zed config is written directly by the tool.
6. For `brain`, the summary reports `missingSections`, outdated section text as `staleSections` and a legacy brain launcher as `legacyLauncher` (its reasons), each named separately. The brain category then works through three calls, each one decision at a time:
   a. `category: "brain"` (after the user's yes) inserts every missing section from the latest bundled template — byte-identical, in the file's line endings — only when the config launches the template's own brain server. It returns `{ outcome: "inserted", inserted }` (markers only; empty when nothing is missing) or `{ outcome: "adapt", adapt, instructions }` naming the sections the user must write for their backend.
   b. `category: "brain"` with `brainChange: <marker | "launcher">` returns one `{ outcome: "change", target, before, after, beforeHash }` diff to show the user. It is read-only. For a non-template config it returns `missing` with the template's version of an absent section instead.
   c. The same call plus that `beforeHash`, only on the user's yes to that one diff, returns `applied`, or a `refused` re-fetch instruction when the bytes changed since the preview.
   Never batch changes under one yes. Every refusal's `instructions` names the next step.

**IMPORTANT — one-at-a-time wizard pattern using AskUserQuestion:**
Do NOT present all categories at once. Walk the user through ONE category at a time using AskUserQuestion with Yes/Skip options. Stop after each question and wait for confirmation before calling with that category.

Categories: pointer-stub, methodology-docs, version-metadata, commands, agents, skills, mcp, ide, readme, brain.

Upgrade surface (user code and user .aide specs are never touched):
- AIDE pointer stub in the agent config file
- Canonical methodology docs under .aide/docs/
- versions.json metadata under .aide/docs/
- Slash commands for all pipeline phases
- Pipeline agent files, skill templates
- MCP server entry in the project's MCP config
- IDE file association config (Zed settings, VS Code extension)
- The user-owned brain config, only through the brain category: missing sections and confirmed migrations, one consented change at a time

Supports Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and Copilot. Auto-detects the framework or accepts an override.

**MCP step:** the canonical aide entry runs the global command `aidemd-mcp`. The entry is read under the `aide` key, or under `aidemd-mcp` when there is no `aide` key; the key is never renamed. Without `targetVersion`, an entry that launches through npx reports `differs` with `globalSwitch: { key, name, installed, installCommand }` and no prescription. Tell the user npx launches time out at session start and ask; on yes, run `installCommand` via Bash first unless `installed` is true (a failed install: say so and stop). Then `category: "mcp"` makes the tool rewrite only that entry's command and args to the global command, every other byte unchanged; it re-checks the global install and, while the package is missing, keeps `differs` and returns `instructions` naming the install command — install, then call again. A missing aide entry returns the global `prescription` plus `globalPackage`; when the package is not installed it also carries `instructions` — act on them: install first, then merge, and never merge after a failed install. An older server cannot switch itself, so a pinned project first moves its pin to a newer version with `targetVersion` (only under the `aide` key; an npx entry under `aidemd-mcp` gets `instructions` to call without `targetVersion` and switch instead) — an exact published `x.y.z`, normally `aide_info`'s `behind.latest`, valid only with no category or with `category: "mcp"`. With it, a local (npx) aide entry is judged by its version pin alone: an older, missing or non-exact pin reports `differs` with `pinMove: { from, to }` (`from` is null when unpinned) and no prescription; a pin at or ahead of the target `matches` and is never moved back. Install the target first (`npx -y @aidemd-mcp/server@{to} sync --help` prints help starting `Usage:` and exits 2 by design; anything else means the install failed — then stop and move nothing). Then `category: "mcp"` with the same `targetVersion` makes the tool write the move itself, changing only the version inside the package argument — the command form, `cmd /c`, `-y`, other servers, formatting and line endings stay byte-identical — and returns `status: "updated"` with `pinMove`. A result that keeps `status: "differs"` with `instructions` means nothing was written (the pin changed since it was checked, the config cannot be edited byte-safely, or the entry is not a locatable `@aidemd-mcp/server` spec): relay the instructions. A global entry is never moved; the target is ignored for it. A moved pin takes effect only in a new session — tell the user to start one. An `aidemd-mcp` entry matches as the bare command or an absolute-path shim of it; a path-launched one may carry `tip`, an informational remark to mention once — never drift, never a merge question. Any other (custom) command under the `aide` key is left alone and reports `matches`. The brain entry is not part of the `mcp` step; a legacy brain launcher is changed only through the brain category's `brainChange: "launcher"` preview and apply, on the user's yes.

beforeHash.description: The `beforeHash` a `brainChange` preview returned. Turns the call into the guarded apply: the change is written only if the current bytes still hash to this value.

brainChange.description: Brain-category-only selector for one stale section (its marker) or the legacy launcher (`launcher`). Without `beforeHash` the call previews that one change read-only; with `beforeHash` it applies it.

category.description: When provided, applies that category. For package-owned categories the call writes all differs/missing files to disk and returns a manifest (no canonicalContent). For `brain` it inserts missing sections (no `brainChange`), previews one change (`brainChange` alone), or applies it (`brainChange` + `beforeHash`); it never rewrites an existing section outside an applied change. When omitted, return all categories as metadata-only summaries (no canonicalContent fields).

framework.description: Force a specific framework instead of auto-detecting. Auto-detection checks for framework-specific files/directories and defaults to Claude Code.

path.description: Custom project root path (defaults to server working directory)

targetVersion.description: Exact published x.y.z version to judge the project's local aide entry's npx pin against (normally aide_info's behind.latest). With category "mcp" the tool moves the pin to it, changing only the version; with no category the move is shown read-only as pinMove. Not valid with any other category. A global entry is never moved.

name: aide_upgrade
